# The Fundamental Laws of Supremacism and Egalitarianism

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026*

## Abstract

This Article articulates two axiomatic principles that characterize sustained conflict at every scale of human organization. The **Fundamental Law of Supremacism** holds that in every system S, sustained conflict SC(C) necessarily implies the existence of a supremacist claim P(Eₓ, Eᵧ) between at least one pair of entities: ∀S, ∀C ⊂ S, SC(C) ⇒ ∃P(Eₓ, Eᵧ). The **Fundamental Law of Egalitarianism** holds that wherever pairwise equality is fully maintained, sustained conflict cannot exist: ∀S, (∀Eₓ, Eᵧ ∈ S, Eql(Eₓ, Eᵧ)) ⇒ ¬SC(C). Both laws are demonstrated through proofs by contradiction.

The laws are context-free: they hold independent of economic conditions, cultural factors, political structures, historical circumstances, technological development, and geographic location. They occupy an axiomatic position in social science analogous to the position foundational laws occupy in natural science — not theories to be tested but principles that define the terms of analysis. Together they form the substrate layer of the broader framework, supplying the claim-independent characterization of conduct as supremacist or egalitarian by means, above any local doctrine.

sections.title: The Madisonian Separation of Powers Objective Compliance Test
sections.description: Joseph D. Kirchner. Recovers Madison's actual framework and derives a six-step objective compliance test for separation-of-powers violations, validated against 36 Supreme Court decisions spanning 154 years (1872–2021) at a 100% correspondence rate.
sections.content_level_1:
# The Madisonian Separation of Powers Objective Compliance Test

## Recovering Constitutional Structure Through Textual Analysis

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026*

## Abstract

For 239 years, the United States has lacked any objective legal definition of what constitutes a "separation of powers violation." The *Youngstown* framework describes zones of presidential power but provides no violation test; formalist approaches categorize powers without defining violations; functionalist approaches employ balancing tests that are inherently subjective. The consequence is that separation-of-powers disputes are resolved by power rather than law.

This Article recovers what Madison actually wrote — "distribution" rather than "separation," "balance" and "check" as sequential operations, and non-delegation as a definitional synonym for separation of powers — and from it derives a six-step objective compliance test any court can apply without subjective policy judgments. The test is validated against 36 Supreme Court decisions spanning 154 years (1872–2021), correctly identifying as unconstitutional every action the Court has invalidated: a 100% correspondence rate. Applied to seven additional questions — tariff delegation, qualified immunity, revenue-bill origination, IEEPA tariff authority, administrative rulemaking, impoundment, and prosecutorial non-prosecution agreements — the test yields unconstitutional in all seven. The Article closes by recovering the equitable standing doctrine necessary to enforce the test.

sections.content_level_1:
# Means, Not Views: The Constitutional Distinction Between Radicalism and Extremism

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar; Pro Se Plaintiff,* Kirchner v. Johnson, *No. 1:25-cv-02735-ACR (D.D.C.) — May 2026*

## Abstract

This Article identifies, defines, and defends a constitutional distinction that American First Amendment doctrine has long carried as an implicit thread but has not articulated as a unified analytical framework: the distinction between **radicalism** and **extremism**, drawn at **means, not views**. Radicalism is a political-doctrinal disposition that challenges conventional positions through constitutional means — speech, association, advocacy, petition, dissent, persuasion, peaceful boycott, electoral mobilization. Extremism is the use of unconstitutional means — violence, true threats, or imminent incitement of unlawful action — to advance a political view. The constitutional line is the means deployed, not the radicality of the view advanced.

The Article develops three claims. **First**, this distinction is the operative principle underlying *Brandenburg v. Ohio*, *NAACP v. Claiborne Hardware Co.*, *Snyder v. Phelps*, and the modern First Amendment canon. **Second**, the framework carries a structural corollary: conventional dispositions may themselves be extremist while remaining conventional — slavery, Jim Crow, and the disenfranchisement of women were conventional dispositions whose enforcement by violent means is now universally recognized as extremism that conventional politics legitimized. **Third**, the contemporary counter-terrorism predicate apparatus — exemplified by the May 2026 *U.S. Counterterrorism Strategy* and the June 2025 House Homeland Security hearing on "Anti-Israel Extremist Groups" — operationalizes an unconstitutional categorical collapse of this distinction.

sections.content_level_1:
# Anchor and Bridge

## A Three-Layer Architecture for Universal Deployment of the Means/Views Distinction in Destinations of Conventional Extremism

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026 (~21,000 words)*

## Abstract

This Article supplies the analytical architecture that connects two prior contributions — the constitutional distinction between radicalism and extremism in *Means, Not Views* and the axiomatic principles of *The Fundamental Laws of Supremacism and Egalitarianism* — into a unified framework for universal constitutional deployment. *Means, Not Views* proposed portability across democratic systems by "substituting local controlling authority." That mechanism works in healthy constitutional democracies but breaks in destinations of *conventional extremism*, where the destination's own constitutional apparatus is itself the supremacist actor and there is no clean local authority to substitute to.

The Article supplies the missing architecture: a three-layer system in which (1) the Laws of Supremacism and Egalitarianism operate as an axiomatic *substrate* that requires no local constitutional system to function; (2) the Means/Views distinction supplies the *operational* legal vocabulary; and (3) international and regional human-rights frameworks (ICCPR Articles 19 and 21, ECHR Article 10, ACHR Article 13, African Charter Article 9, and the Special Rapporteur mandates) supply the *remedial* channel. It develops a survey instrument for characterizing state action independent of local doctrine and a bridging function explaining why international standards bind analytically, then applies the architecture to polities with ratified-but-defected obligations, polities without ratified obligations, and polities in transition.

# Applied Diagnostics

## Structural Analysis of Active Conflicts Through the Bodily-Jurisdiction Framework

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026*

## Abstract

This Article is a repository of *applied* diagnostics, distinct from the framework brief's *structural* theory. Where *Bodily Jurisdiction* articulates the architecture (object → substrate → floor → fractal imperative → social-contract conditional → floor-protection doctrines → intervention warrant → remedial channel), this Article deploys that architecture against specific real-world conflicts.

A seven-step template is applied to each case: (1) civil-capacity inventory; (2) internal exclusivity diagnostic; (3) external exclusivity diagnostic; (4) catalog of floor violations; (5) meta-violation analysis; (6) intervention-warrant assessment; and (7) the congruent egalitarian path. The diagnostic does not pick winners, resolve substantive policy disputes, predict timelines, or supply political will — its contribution is structural diagnostic clarity, and it operates symmetrically across parties, producing the same kind of finding regardless of which party the analyst sympathizes with.

sections.title: Bodily Jurisdiction: The Floor of Constitutional Authority
sections.description: Joseph D. Kirchner. Restates bodily autonomy structurally rather than as a balanceable right: the body is a sovereign jurisdictional sphere and the floor of the constitutional architecture, the primary sovereignty from which all higher-level authority is derivative.
sections.content_level_1:
# Bodily Jurisdiction: The Floor of Constitutional Authority

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026*

## Abstract

Bodily autonomy is conventionally argued as a *right* — privacy, substantive due process, equal protection — susceptible to balancing against the state's interests. This framework restates the argument *structurally*: the body is a sovereign jurisdictional sphere analogous to a state's territorial sphere. The state cannot regulate inside the bodily sphere not because the regulation would interfere with a balanceable interest, but because the regulation operates *outside the state's jurisdiction in the first place*. The state's interest never enters the analysis until its action crosses the jurisdictional line.

This is a categorically different posture from the *Roe*/*Casey*/*Dobbs* tradition: it does not depend on the substantive merit of the bodily decision, only on whether the state's regulatory hand has crossed the structural boundary. Bodily jurisdiction at the individual human level is the **floor** of the entire jurisdictional hierarchy — the primary sovereignty from which all higher-level authority (local, state, federal, international) is derivative — and it integrates with the Means/Views framework, which operates above the floor as a domain-specific protective doctrine.

sections.content_level_1:
# Torture in the Codified Democratic Order

## The May 2026 Sumud Flotilla and the Three-Level Meta-Violation

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026 (~11,500 words)*

## Abstract

On the night of May 18, 2026, the Israeli Navy intercepted the Global Sumud Flotilla approximately seventy to eighty nautical miles off Cyprus, in international waters far beyond any conceivable Israeli territorial claim. Forces boarded forty-one vessels flying the flags of more than forty states, seized humanitarian cargo bound for Gaza, and transferred 428–430 detainees to Ketziot prison, where they were subjected to documented torture and cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment authorized at the ministerial level. Flag states summoned ambassadors and issued condemnations while declining to execute the legal warrants their codified obligations supply.

This Article uses the Sumud case to demonstrate the three-level meta-violation structure of the codified democratic order — direct floor violation, rhetorical inversion, and deference-based non-execution — and argues that the conduct triggers mandatory universal jurisdiction under Article 7 of the Convention Against Torture. Once torture is on the record, the flag states' deference is no longer discretionary; it is a direct breach of the *aut dedere aut judicare* obligation, enforceable under *Belgium v. Senegal*, graduating the structural critique into a treaty-law claim binding on every state party to the Convention.

## Read the full Article

sections.content_level_1:
# The Rejection of Law

## Treaty Defection, State Secession, and the Fractal Constitution

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026 (~14,000 words)*

## Abstract

In 2002, Undersecretary of State John Bolton "unsigned" the Rome Statute — an act with no analog in the Vienna Convention or constitutional law, created by unilateral executive fiat. In 1869, *Texas v. White* held the Union "perpetual" and "indissoluble": a state cannot unilaterally secede, because the federal constitutional order is constituted by its binding character over its members.

This Article argues these two propositions cannot stand together as principled constitutional law. The principle that forbids state secession at the federal-state interface is structurally identical to the principle the Bolton unsigning violates at the federal-international interface; enforcing it downward while exempting the federal executive upward is a particularized-enforcement violation at the structural level. The Article reconstructs four decades of U.S. and Israeli unilateral declarations of unbinding and develops four independent doctrinal grounds against the practice — Supremacy Clause, inferior-officer *expressio unius*, war-powers, and structural-fractal — converging on the conclusion that asymmetric enforcement of the binding principle is constitutionally indefensible.

sections.title: The Declaration of Humanity: An Inclusive Definition and Its Operational Necessity
sections.description: Joseph D. Kirchner. Shifts from assertion-form articulations of universal rights to a definitional-form premise — humanity is every person, family, people, and nation, without exception — which is invulnerable to the redescription mechanism through which regimes of organized exclusion operate.
sections.content_level_1:
# The Declaration of Humanity

## An Inclusive Definition and Its Operational Necessity

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026*

## Abstract

This Declaration articulates a foundational definitional premise grounding the codified democratic order at every scale: humanity is every person, every family, every people, and every nation — without exception, without precondition, without diminution at any scale. The shift from the assertion-form articulation of universal rights ("all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights") to the definitional-form articulation ("humanity is the inclusive whole at every scale") is structurally consequential. Assertion-form articulations are vulnerable to *redescription* — the supremacist's denial that an excluded group falls within the asserted category, the mechanism through which every historical regime of organized exclusion has operated. Definitional-form articulations are invulnerable to redescription, because to deny any member's humanity is to deny the definition itself.

Humanity, on this definition, is constitutive and not forfeitable: no party, by any conduct, can divest itself or another of membership. What violation forfeits is the reciprocal cooperation other members extend, while activating collective self-defense and — for crimes against humanity — the right of all members to defend humanity itself. The doctrines of *jus cogens* obligations *erga omnes*, universal jurisdiction over atrocity crimes, and the Responsibility to Protect are downstream operational expressions of this foundation.

sections.title: The Ratification Protocol: A Two-Stage Architecture for Member Commitment
sections.description: Joseph D. Kirchner. sections.content_level_1:
# The Ratification Protocol

## A Two-Stage Architecture for Member Commitment to the Codified Democratic Order

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026*

## Abstract

The Ratification Protocol operationalizes the Declaration of Humanity's foundational premise into a procedural mechanism by which polities affirm — or restore — their membership in the codified democratic order. Its architecture rests on four structural commitments. *First,* ratification proceeds in two stages: a Stage 1 Member Commitment Declaration; a grace period during which the polity adjusts local laws through its own constitutional process; certification of compliance by a deliberative body of existing members; and a Stage 2 Full Ratification Declaration. *Second,* sovereignty is preserved at every stage through retention of per-situation national-level enforcement; the framework neither has nor seeks supranational coercive infrastructure. *Third,* the operational disposition is patience over coercion. *Fourth,* enforcement consists of four structural mechanisms operating together: coherent dialogue, the alliance of members, collective self-defense rights, and the defense-of-humanity right against atrocity crimes.

The two-stage architecture resolves the enforcement problem (structural rather than institutional), the sovereignty problem (ratification by the polity's own deliberative process), the reservation problem (certification against the structural test), and the variety problem (first ratification, full-compliance ratification, and restoration by defecting members all handled through one process).

sections.content_level_1:
# The Board of Peace

## An Operational Anatomy of USURPATION at the International Scale

*Joseph D. Kirchner — Independent Scholar — May 2026*

## Abstract

The Declaration of Humanity supplies the foundational definitional premise; the Ratification Protocol supplies the certification standard; the Madisonian Compliance Test supplies the diagnostic apparatus; the Rejection of Law analysis supplies the four-decade defection pattern; the Sumud Flotilla article supplies the three-level meta-violation diagnosis. The Board of Peace is the operational case that tests all of them — a violation arriving with a logo, a master plan, founding donors, a UN Security Council endorsement, and international legal personality.

Applying the corpus's diagnostic apparatus to the Board's formal instruments (the Charter of January 16, 2026; UNSC Resolution 2803; the founding-donor and founding-contributor declarations; the FIFA memorandum; and the Davos presentation), the structural verdict is unambiguous. The architecture operates the dual Power Separation Vulnerability: paradigm USURPATION at the international scale by the Board of Peace (grounded in the Chairman position of Charter Article 3.2), paired with paradigm ABDICATION by the UN Security Council, whose Resolution 2803 supplies operational space rather than exercising the Council's own constitutive authority. The Board fails every feature of the Ratification Protocol's certification standard, and the Council's "welcome" is not a cure but the structurally complementary abdication by which the violation operates.
